messages:
alina: Quick design review — thinking through the 'panic' action in the rollout timeline. Current mock shows a red hard-button labelled 'Rollback now'. Feels aggressive, and I'm worried voiceover users will miss the confirmation context. Thoughts?

jon: I agree about the label. From an engineering POV we also need to ensure the action is debounced/atomic. But copy-wise maybe make it two-step: primary action toggles 'Safe rollback' (non-destructive preview) and the destructive button hidden behind a menu.

miriam: A11y nit: screen reader will read button text verbatim. "Rollback now" could be misread without context. Recommend using aria-label that includes intent + scope, e.g., "Rollback current release to previous stable version, opens confirmation dialog". Also add role="alert" to the toast after rollback completes.

sam: UX question: do we want 'Safe rollback' to be the default primary? That might help accidental clicks but could make the workflow longer for SREs who want immediate revert. Maybe expose keyboard shortcut + confirm for experts?

jon: Proposal: primary CTA = 'Revert to previous' (less emotive), secondary menu -> 'Force rollback (no-canary)' for power users. Add a short tooltip on hover: "Reverts traffic to previous version; preserves release notes and metrics."

alina: Wire suggestion: show a compact timeline scrubber with an inline kebab menu per snapshot. Kebab contains 'Preview revert' and 'Force revert'. For keyboard users the kebab must be reachable via tab and open with Enter/Space.

miriam: Also timeline scrubbing announcements — when keyboard focus moves through versions, screen reader should say: "Version v1.4 — deployed 2 days ago — traffic 20% — preview available". Use aria-live="polite" for that region. Avoid aria-live="assertive" to not interrupt typing.

alina: Good call. Also visual affordance: canaries currently shown as overlapping bars. Can we add hatching patterns in addition to color so high-contrast mode works?

jon: Yes, we can add CSS patterns. Example snippet for high-contrast fallback:

```css
.canary-1 { background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px); }
.canary-2 { background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.06) 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px); }
```

miriam: Nice. Also ensure focus outline is visible when using patterned fills: outline-color must contrast with both pattern and background. Use high-contrast tokens.

sam: Microcopy around undo: current toast says 'Rollback in progress'. Could we change to 'Rollback started — click to view progress or undo'? Makes the action discoverable.

alina: I like that. One more thing: when a user initiates 'Preview revert', we show a diffside peek. Need to add an ARIA quick link: 'Press p to open preview' for keyboard discoverability. But avoid global shortcuts that conflict.

jon: I'll add an in-component help dot that lists local shortcuts. And implement a settings flag to enable power shortcuts.

devops-bot: deploy-check: new UI changes will require e2e tests for keyboard navigation and a11y smoke. Queue job #5824. :white_check_mark:

miriam: Final a11y checklist for this thread: 1) aria-labels for destructive controls, 2) aria-live polite for scrubber, 3) visible focus outlines for patterned canaries, 4) confirmation dialogs trap focus and include rationale.

alina: Thanks — I'll update the mock and push a small prototype to figma. tagging @jon for CSS handoff and @miriam for accessibility review after prototype.
